meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'absent'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Notre directeur est absent du bureau toute la semaine.
examples.trans: Our director is absent from the office all week.

examples.text: Il avait l'air complètement absent pendant la réunion.
examples.trans: He looked completely spaced out during the meeting.

meanings.note: With things and places. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to like'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aimé').
With people. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to like'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'aimé').

examples.text: Tu n'aimais pas Mandelieu? C'est un bel endroit.
examples.trans: Didn't you like Mandelieu? It's a lovely place.

meanings.note: à + le contracted: au boulot, au téléphone

examples.trans: I've got a problem at work.

meanings.note: Neutral, polite. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'goodbye', common in natural conversation.
À bientôt = see you soon. Invariable French adverb meaning 'soon'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
as a form of address: chéri (to a man), chérie (to a woman)
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'darling'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Ça va, chérie? Tu es en retard.

meanings.note: Ma chérie = my dear, darling. Feminine noun ('la chérie', plural 'les chéries') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'darling'.

examples.text: Oui, ma chérie? Qu'est-ce qui ne va pas?
examples.trans: Yes, my dear? What is wrong?

meanings.note: je suis désolé(e) = I'm sorry; désolé! alone also works
en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: Ma fille = my daughter. Feminine noun ('la fille', plural 'les filles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'daughter'.
Une petite fille = a little girl. Feminine noun ('la fille', plural 'les filles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'daughter'.

examples.trans: I want to see my daughter.

examples.text: Je veux voir ma fille, voyager.
examples.trans: I want to see my daughter, to travel.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: laisser quelqu'un voir = to let someone see
Laisse-moi = let me. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to leave'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'laissé').

examples.text: Laissez vos photos et votre CV ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos and your CV here.

meanings.note: Mais oui! = of course!. French conjunction meaning 'but', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
Laisser un message. Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'message, text'.

examples.text: Désolé pour tes messages. J'ai été très occupé.
examples.trans: Sorry about your messages. I've been very busy.

meanings.note: Stressed form: pour moi, avec moi. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'me'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: ma before a feminine noun, mon before a vowel

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: pardonnez-moi = forgive me (formal)

examples.text: Pardonnez-moi, mais je ne parle pas de ça.
examples.trans: Forgive me, but I don't talk about that.

meanings.en: to please, to be liked by
meanings.note: Ça me plaît = I like it. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to please'.

meanings.en: s'il vous plaît / s'il te plaît = please
meanings.note: Formal / informal. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to please'.

examples.text: S'il vous plaît. Il n'y a rien entre Mathias et moi, d'accord?
examples.trans: Please. There's nothing between Mathias and me, okay?

prier.gloss: to pray, beg; je vous en prie = please

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to pray'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'prié').

examples.text: Bonjour Catherine, entrez, je vous en prie.
Je t'en prie, je comprends parfaitement.

meanings.en: to call back, to phone again
meanings.note: Rappeler quelque chose à quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to call back'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'rappelé').

Rappeler quelque chose à quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to call back'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'rappelé').

examples.text: Oui. Je suis presque au point. Je vous rappelle.
examples.trans: Yes. I've almost got it. I'll call you back.

meanings.en: to regret, to be sorry for
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to regret'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'regretté').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to regret'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'regretté').

examples.text: Christophe le regrette aussi. Il t'admire, tu le sais!
examples.trans: Christophe regrets it too. He admires you, you know that!

meanings.note: On se reverra: we'll meet again. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Prefix 're-'/'ré-' marks repetition, return, or intensity. Core French verb meaning 'to see again'.
Literally 'until seeing again'. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Prefix 're-'/'ré-' marks repetition, return, or intensity. Core French verb meaning 'to see again'.

examples.trans: I want to see this film again.

meanings.note: Répondre à quelqu'un. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Prefix 'ré-' marks repetition, return, or intensity. Core French verb meaning 'to answer'.
Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Prefix 'ré-' marks repetition, return, or intensity. Core French verb meaning 'to answer'.

examples.trans: I have to answer the phone.

examples.text: Je suis désolé. Je dois répondre, c'est urgent.
examples.trans: I'm sorry. I have to answer, it's urgent.

meanings.note: formal or plural; casual: s'il te plaît

examples.text: Réservez-moi un massage, s'il vous plaît.

meanings.note: Si tu veux = if you want. French conjunction meaning 'if', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
answering a negative question: Aucune nouvelle? - Si!

examples.text: Si tu veux, on peut en parler demain matin.
examples.trans: If you want, we can talk about it tomorrow morning.

examples.text: Dis-moi tout de suite si le rôle t'intéresse.
examples.trans: Tell me right away if the role interests you.

meanings.note: casual object pronoun, before the verb

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
Je ne sais pas. Je voulais te faire la surprise.
examples.trans: I don't know. I wanted to surprise you.

meanings.note: Tout le monde = everybody. Spoken French det expression meaning 'all', common in natural conversation.

meanings.en: tout ce que = all that, everything that
meanings.note: Pronoun use. Spoken French det expression meaning 'all', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: C'est tout ce que je peux faire.
Désolé, c'est tout ce que je peux faire.
examples.trans: Sorry, that's all I can do.

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: Place: à Paris, à mon cours. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
meanings.note: Contractions. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
The most common verb. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
Ce + est. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
